## LANDED — change 1117 merged as `2a3abe6abde981fe575728b58043b6c06baa7136`

Gates: **LLM-Review +1** (17:59, PASS, 1 advisory/non-blocking finding, no inline comments) and
**Verified +1** (17:30, CI SUCCESS, run 30649890441), 0 unresolved comments. Submitted 18:01:24.

The merged SHA differs from the pushed one (`014a1362d` -> `2a3abe6ab`) because `main` is
Rebase-If-Necessary and Gerrit rebased server-side. Verified the rebase preserved everything:
`git diff 014a1362d 2a3abe6ab` over all three files is **empty** (content byte-identical,
319 insertions / 37 deletions), and the merged commit carries the intact
`rebar-ticket: 5546-65da-f42a-4cce` trailer, its `Change-Id`, and the DCO sign-off.

Note for anyone landing a change here: `git merge --ff-only origin/main` **cannot** work after
a Gerrit submit — `014a1362d` is provably not an ancestor of `2a3abe6ab`, so the fast-forward
is impossible by construction, and `origin` (the GitHub mirror) lags besides. Fetch
`gerrit main` and `reset --hard` your own worktree to the merged SHA instead. Never
fast-forward or reset the shared main checkout.

## The WU-2 behaviour change was DELIBERATE — not an accidental test relaxation

Two tests from epic 97e7 / P1.4 (WU-2) previously pinned *union-merging an unrelated history
that carries local ticket events*. **They now expect a REFUSAL instead. This is the operator's
explicit decision, recorded on this ticket before implementation, not a test being relaxed to
fit a fix.** The decision is: **self-heal, but only when safe** — union-merge when the local
store is a genuine divergent copy of the shared tracker (shared ancestry, or an empty local
store with nothing to lose), and when it looks like an accidentally-created ORPHAN store
instead, do NOT merge: report DIVERGED and leave recovery to an explicit operator action. The
predicate deliberately fails toward reporting DIVERGED, never toward silently absorbing an
orphan store into the shared tickets branch.

Why this is not a weakening: WU-2's actual data-safety invariant is *no local commit is ever
discarded/orphaned, so a serial `git gc` stays safe*. Refusing discards strictly LESS than
merging did, so that invariant is preserved and strengthened — and both tests still assert it
(reachability from HEAD, survival of `gc --prune=now`). Only the mechanism assertion flipped,
and every removed assertion was replaced by its exact logical inverse rather than by a weaker
check; the gc test additionally traded `cat-file -e` for the stronger `merge-base --is-ancestor`
reachability assertion. The union path itself remains covered end-to-end (empty-orphan adopt,
and the shared-ancestry diverged merge) in `tests/unit/test_sync_narrow_refspec.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — the data decision is recorded on this ticket (self-heal only when safe;
      predicate + rationale in the decision comment above).
- [x] **AC2** — sync fetches with an explicit refspec, and the two-clone/narrow-refspec test
      proves an already-divergent store reconverges with no event loss in either direction.
      Measured end-to-end through `rebar list` in a real single-branch clone: 0/0/0 tickets
      before, 2/2/2 after.
- [x] **AC3 (adapted)** — sync is no longer inert, but its remaining refusal is deliberate and
      REPORTED: a `DIVERGED` warning naming `rebar fsck` / `rebar fsck-recover`, with the
      rationale documented at the predicate in `sync.py`.

## Close class: `env_integration`

The defect is an incorrect assumption about the **git CLI integration contract** — that a bare
`git fetch <remote> <branch>` updates `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` — which holds only when
the remote's configured refspec covers that branch, and therefore fails **only in a specific
environment**: a narrow/single-branch clone. Not `regression` (nothing previously working
broke). Not `plan_defect` (the design — union-merge on divergence — was right; only its
reachability was broken). `preexisting` is also literally true but far less informative, since
it would apply to almost any dedicated bug ticket.

## Follow-up (not in scope here)

Sibling sweep filed as **35f7-a39d-8e27-4922** (linked `discovered_from`): the same bare-fetch
pattern is still live in `push.py:182` and in the reconcile-bridge workflows, where it is a
strong candidate root cause for bug **449f-f9bf-be90-47fe**.
